channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Em seu 3º mandato, Lula acumula 124 entrevistas exclusivas
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has given 124 exclusive interviews since the start of his third term in 2023, peaking in 2024 with 43 interviews. In 2026, an election year, he has conducted 17 interviews in the first half—12 with Brazilian outlets and 5 with foreign media—where television accounted for the largest share. His media strategy aligns with heightened public appearances tied to infrastructure deliveries, social program launches, and domestic and international travel amid the electoral contest.

item.title: Lula teria 48,8% dos votos contra 42,3% de Flávio no 2º turno, aponta pesquisa Atlas
item.description: The Atlas/Bloomberg poll shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva leading with 48.8% of voting intentions against 42.3% for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical runoff, maintaining a 6.5-point lead. Lula also leads in all first-round scenarios tested.

item.title: Lula pode gravar inserção com Jerônimo, Jaques e Rui em meio à crise do Master
item.description: President Lula may record electoral inserts alongside Bahia Governor Jerônimo Rodrigues, Minister of the Civil House Rui Costa, and Senator Jaques Wagner during his visit to Salvador this Wednesday (July 1st). The decision will be made after his arrival in the state, and the material aims to support PT allies amid Jaques Wagner's political crisis linked to the Banco Master investigation.

item.title: Lula dobra a sua vantagem sobre Flávio no 1º turno, mostra pesquisa AtlasIntel/Bloomberg
item.description: Lula doubles his lead over Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round, increasing from a 5-point gap in April to nearly 10 points in June, with 46.3% versus 36.6%. In the second-round simulation, Lula leads 48.8% to 42.3%, reversing the technical tie from April. The poll reflects the impact of the Bolsonaro clan’s internal crisis, following a critical video by Michelle Bolsonaro against her stepson Flávio.

item.title: Aécio Neves é rejeitado por 54% dos eleitores, diz pesquisa
item.description: An AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll released on July 1, 2026 shows Aécio Neves (PSDB) with 54% rejection, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 53% and Lula (PT) at 48.6%. Aécio and Flávio are technically tied within the 1 percentage point margin of error. The survey interviewed 4,999 people nationwide from June 26–30, 2026, with 95% confidence and TSE registration BR-04582/2026.

item.title: Julho traz restrições a candidatos à reeleição em anúncios de obras
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has barred pre-candidates running for re-election from participating in public works inaugurations starting this Saturday (July 5), aiming to ensure equal conditions in the 2026 elections. São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) accelerated deliveries such as the Line 6-Orange subway and Washington Luís station on Line 17-Gold before the deadline, noting that while he cannot personally inaugurate projects, his secretaries may do so on behalf of the government. He has invested an extra R$ 3.7 billion in the Orange Line’s first phase but keeps documents justifying the additional cost under secrecy.

item.title: Lula é aprovado por 45,9% e desaprovado por 52,3%, diz pesquisa
item.description: The AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll conducted from June 26 to 30, 2026 shows that 45.9% of Brazilian voters approve of President Lula’s administration, while 52.3% disapprove, with a 1 percentage point margin of error. Only 39.7% rate the government as 'good' or 'excellent', compared to 48.3% who view it as 'bad' or 'terrible'. The survey took place shortly after the ninth phase of Operation Compliance Zero, which targeted Lula’s ally Jaques Wagner, former Senate government leader.

item.title: Renan Santos cresce na AtlasIntel, mas menos do que campanha esperava
item.description: Renan Santos registers 7.8% voting intention in the latest AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll, a 0.9-point increase since May, within the margin of error. The growth fell short of campaign expectations, which had tracked him at 8% to 9%. Lula leads with 46.3%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 36.6% and Santos in third.

item.title: Rui Costa e Jaques Wagner lideram corrida ao Senado na Bahia
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey released on July 1, 2026 shows Rui Costa (PT) leading the Bahia Senate race with 50.6% voting intentions, followed by Jaques Wagner (PT) at 36.7%. Conducted between June 27–30 among 1,500 respondents across 64 municipalities in Bahia, the poll has a 2.6 percentage point margin of error and 95% confidence level. Registered with the TSE under BA-04848/2026, the study cost R$45,000 and was funded by Bahia Notícias.

item.title: AtlasIntel: 52,3% desaprovam Lula. 48,3% acham governo ruim ou péssimo
item.description: According to an AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll released on July 1, 52.3% of Brazilian voters disapprove of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government, while 45.9% approve and 1.8% are undecided. Disapproval has risen slightly from April (53%) and March (54%) after a period of decline from June to December last year. The government is rated as 'bad' or 'terrible' by 48.3% of respondents, with the worst ratings among 16-24 year olds (61.9%) and the best among those over 60 (50.4% rating it 'good' or 'excellent').

item.title: Lula amplia vantagem sobre Flávio Bolsonaro em nova rodada da AtlasIntel
item.description: Lula expands his lead over Flávio Bolsonaro to 11 percentage points in the first round, according to the AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll released July 1, with 47.2% versus 36.2%. Renan Santos emerges for the first time in sole third place with 7.8%, while government approval dropped to 45.9%. In a runoff, Lula defeats all opponents, leading Bolsonaro by 6.5 points.

item.title: Ministros de Lula deram 267 entrevistas no 1º semestre de 2026
item.description: In the first half of 2026, the 38 ministers of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government granted 267 exclusive interviews, while Lula himself gave 17 individual interviews to the media. First Lady Janja Lula da Silva was interviewed twice. Minister of the General Secretariat of the Presidency, Guilherme Boulos (Psol), led with 42 interviews, surpassing the president in media exposure. Seventeen ministers who left office during the period gave 52 interviews, with former Finance Minister Fernando Haddad and former Chief of Staff Rui Costa each recording seven. Seven ministers did not give any exclusive interviews.

item.title: ACM Neto lidera disputa pelo governo da Bahia no 1º turno
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey released on July 1, 2026, shows ACM Neto (União Brasil) leading the Bahia gubernatorial race with 49.2% voting intention in the first round, ahead of incumbent Governor Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT) at 37.5%. The poll interviewed 1,500 people across 64 municipalities from June 27–30, 2026, with a 2.6 percentage point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Em ano eleitoral, Lula dá 17 entrevistas exclusivas
item.description: In the first half of 2026, President Lula granted 17 exclusive interviews, slightly more than in the same period of 2025 (16) but fewer than in 2024 (21), despite the election year. Interviews were predominantly with Brazilian outlets (12), including international media such as The Washington Post and El País. Lula maintained a similar interview rhythm to 2025, emphasizing social program announcements and retaining a lead in polls over his main rival, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Jogos de hoje, quarta, 1º de julho: onde assistir futebol ao vivo e horários
item.description: On Wednesday, July 1, 2026, the FIFA World Cup 2026 will feature three key matches: England vs. Democratic Republic of the Congo at 1:00 PM (CazéTV), Belgium vs. Senegal at 5:00 PM (TV Globo, SBT, Sportv, N Sports, ge tv, CazéTV), and United States vs. Bosnia and Herzegovina at 9:00 PM (CazéTV). The content mentions Neymar, Lula, and Cristiano Ronaldo as figures involved in tournament controversies, but there is no direct connection to the 2026 Brazilian elections.

item.title: Justiça italiana analisa extradição de Carla Zambelli no caso da perseguição com arma de fogo
item.description: Italian justice has begun the extradition hearing for former deputy Carla Zambelli over illegal firearm possession and unlawful coercion with a weapon, stemming from a 2022 incident in São Paulo where she chased a man while armed. Zambelli did not attend the hearing in Rome. Minister Gilmar Mendes of Brazil’s STF previously sent assurances to Italy, affirming the conviction’s validity by wide majorities (9-2 and 10-1) and stating the process was regular and free of defects that would block extradition.

item.title: Podcast: o peso de Minas Gerais na eleição e a indefinição de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro no estado
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro visited Minas Gerais in June, highlighting their struggles to secure strong support in the state, which is Brazil’s second-largest electoral college and historically pivotal for national victory. Despite their visits, neither managed to establish a solid electoral base in Minas, reflecting the state’s fragmented politics and unpredictable voter behavior.

item.title: PT e PL ignoram legislação eleitoral e impulsionam críticas a opositores
item.description: The PL and PT violated electoral law by boosting attacks against opponents on social media, spending at least R$277,000 and reaching over 39.1 million impressions. This practice, prohibited by Electoral Justice, aims to amplify negative content against electoral rivals. The case occurs in the context of Brazil’s 2026 elections.

item.title: Como fica o mapa do metrô de SP com a inauguração da Linha 6-Laranja
item.description: The first section of São Paulo's Line 6-Orange metro line opens after an eight-year delay, featuring six stations. Service begins on July 2 with limited weekday hours and no fare collection during this assisted operation phase. The metropolitan transport map will be updated to include the new stations and the Washington Luís station on Line 17-Gold, which introduces Brazil's first 'Y'-shaped rail configuration.

item.title: Empresários do agro paulista doam R$ 1 milhão para partido de Tarcísio
item.description: São Paulo agribusiness entrepreneurs donated nearly R$1 million to the Republicans party in June, ahead of party conventions, to support Governor Tarcísio de Freitas’ campaign, which has offered land regularization and fiscal benefits to the sector. The largest contribution came from Luiz Zillo Neto (Usina Quatá) with R$350,000, followed by Carlos Dinucci and Antonio Eduardo Tonielo Filho, each donating R$100,000. Among the donors is João Luiz Quagliato Neto, convicted in 2023 for slave labor on a farm in Pará.

item.title: Craques do Cruzeiro convocam torcida para jogão contra Grêmio no DF
item.description: Cruzeiro and Grêmio will face off in a preparatory friendly on July 12 at 5:00 PM at Arena Mané Garrincha in Brasília, organized by Metrópoles Sports. Stars Fagner and Lucas Silva urged fans to attend, while striker Kaio Jorge, who has scored 45 goals in 95 appearances for Cruzeiro since joining from Juventus in 2024, is highlighted as one of Brazil’s top attackers and aims for the 2026 scoring title. Tickets are now available for the match.

item.title: Dosimetria, Uberização e mais: STF encerra semestre em sessão nesta quarta e casos de repercussão devem ficar para agosto, veja lista
item.description: The STF concludes its semester with the final session of judgments this Wednesday (1st), focusing on the validity of provisions in the Administrative Improbity Law. High-repercussion cases — including 'Uberization' (worker-platform relations), 'Dosimetry' (reduced penalties for antidemocratic acts), and Rio de Janeiro succession — are postponed until August after the recess. Rapporteur Alexandre de Moraes maintained the suspension of the Dosimetry Law, while the PGR opposed this measure.

item.title: Advogado do Prerrogativas vai coordenar campanha de Lula em SP
item.description: Marco Aurélio de Carvalho, a founding member of the Prerrogativas group, has been appointed to coordinate Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's re-election campaign in São Paulo. He will also support Fernando Haddad’s bid for state governor, aligning the national campaign with the state-level race. Aurélio stated that São Paulo is decisive for Lula’s victory and highlighted the strength and experience of the PT ticket.

item.title: PL aciona TSE contra Lula por discurso de ódio e racismo em SC
item.description: The PL filed a representation with the TSE against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, alleging he spread hate speech and racism against Santa Catarina’s population during an official event in Itajaí, and engaged in premature electoral propaganda. The petition requests fines, a ban on repeating such statements, and referral to the Electoral Prosecutor’s Office and the Attorney General’s Office. The Planalto has not yet issued an official response.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro foi convencida a não se desfiliar do PL e disputa ao Senado está mantida, dizem aliadas
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro was persuaded by allies not to leave the PL and to maintain her Senate candidacy in the Federal District. Although she announced her resignation as head of PL Women to focus on caring for her husband, Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest, she decided to stay in the party after meeting with Valdemar Costa Neto and receiving support from female leaders. The decision comes amid tensions with her stepson, Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL’s pre-candidate for president.

item.title: Kassio deve congelar teto de gastos de campanhas a pedido de partidos
item.description: The president of the TSE, Kassio Nunes Marques, is expected to comply with a request from party leaders to freeze campaign spending caps for the 2026 elections at the same level set for 2022, without inflation adjustment. This would limit financial transfers to candidates, keeping spending limits static despite rising costs.

item.title: Lula terá reencontro com Jaques Wagner na Bahia 2 semanas após crise com operação da PF
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will arrive in Bahia this Wednesday (1st) for a series of inaugurations, two weeks after removing Senator Jaques Wagner from his position as Senate government leader. The meeting marks a reunion between Lula and his long-time ally, following the crisis triggered by a Federal Police operation that led to Wagner’s removal. The visit is part of broader efforts to rebuild the governing coalition in the Northeast.

item.title: Lula cita o volante Casemiro para dizer que governo pode fazer mais
item.description: President Lula cited Brazilian midfielder Casemiro during the launch of the 2026/2027 Family Farming Harvest Plan to argue that the government can achieve more than it currently is, using the analogy of a player criticized in the first half who scored the equalizing goal and helped secure victory. He announced R$ 97.3 billion for the plan, with R$ 85.2 billion allocated to Pronaf — nearly 9% higher than the previous cycle — emphasizing support for family agriculture.

item.title: TSE deixa de julgar recurso de candidato mais votado em Roraima à espera do STF
item.description: The TSE unanimously suspended the judgment of the appeal of the most voted candidate in Roraima's supplementary gubernatorial election, Arthur Henrique (PL), awaiting the STF's ruling on desincompatibilization validity. Henrique, who won 60.87% of valid votes, had his candidacy initially rejected by the TRE-RR for resigning as mayor less than three months before the election, violating the Clean Record Law. The TSE's decision awaits the STF's ruling on RCL 94894 and ADI 7942, concerning the rules for interim governorship.

item.title: PT oficializará candidatura de Lula à reeleição em 2 de agosto
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) will officially nominate Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for re-election on August 2 in São Paulo, with Geraldo Alckmin as his running mate. The first round is scheduled for October 4, 2026, with a potential runoff on October 25. Lula aims for a historic fourth term, and the PT will receive R$ 615 million from the Electoral Fund in 2026 — the second-largest allocation among parties, surpassed only by the PL.

item.title: A decisão do TSE sobre cassação do ex-governador de Roraima
item.description: The TSE upheld the annulment of the mandates of former Governor Antonio Denarium and former Vice-Governor Edilson Damião for abuse of power during the 2022 campaign, ordering new elections in Roraima. The supplementary elections held on June 21 saw Arthur Henrique (PL) as the top vote-getter, but his candidacy was rejected by the Electoral Justice, leaving the final outcome to be decided by the TSE.

item.title: TSE mantém decisão que cassou mandato de Denarium, ex-governador de RR
item.description: The TSE confirmed the cassation of the mandates of former Roraima governor Antonio Denarium and former vice-governor Edilson Damião due to abuse of power during the 2022 campaign, including irregular distribution of basic food baskets and housing repair aid. The unanimous decision rejected the defense's appeal, upholding their ineligibility and ordering new elections in the state.

item.title: Fux comandará Turma do STF responsável por processo do Master
item.description: Minister Luiz Fux will assume the presidency of the STF's 2nd Chamber in August, replacing Gilmar Mendes, and defended ministers' independence in voting. The chamber handles high-impact cases, including the Master Bank case and the debate on private contracts replacing public deeds in real estate. The change is administrative and does not affect case rapporteurs or outcomes.

item.title: O que é o PL Mulher, setorial do partido que Michelle Bolsonaro presidiu por 3 anos
item.description: The PL Women's Bureau is the female wing of the Liberal Party (PL), established to encourage women's political participation and support female candidacies. Michelle Bolsonaro led the bureau for three years, from 2023 until her resignation on April 30, 2025, citing family care duties and tensions with her stepson Flávio Bolsonaro. The bureau provides training in communication, legislative work, and conservative ideology, emphasizing family, faith, and patriotism.

item.title: TSE suspende prazo sobre diplomação para governador na eleição suplementar de Roraima
item.description: The TSE suspended the judgment of appeals regarding the candidacy registrations of Arthur Henrique and Subtenente Veltom in the supplementary election for governor of Roraima, awaiting a definitive ruling from the STF on the disqualification deadline. It also suspended the regional calendar deadline for the certification of elected officials. The decision was unanimous, with Minister Antonio Carlos Ferreira emphasizing the need to await the STF to avoid contradictory legal pronouncements.

item.title: TSE nega recursos e mantém cassação de governador de Roraima
item.description: The TSE upheld the removal of former Roraima governor Antônio Denarium and former vice-governor Edilson Damião for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections, confirming their eight-year ineligibility. Despite Denarium’s resignation to run for Senate, the TSE ordered new direct elections held on June 21, where Arthur Henrique (PL) won 60.87% of valid votes, although his candidacy was later rejected by Roraima’s Electoral Justice, leaving the final outcome to be decided by the TSE.

item.title: TSE vai esperar decisão do Supremo sobre eleição suplementar de RR
item.description: The TSE decided to await the STF's final ruling on the validity of the 2026 supplementary election calendar before certifying Arthur Henrique's (PL) victory in Roraima, which occurred under sub judice conditions following the removal of Governor Antonio Denarium. Although rapporteur Antonio Carlos Ferreira acknowledged jurisprudence permitting shortened incompatibilization periods in supplementary elections, he urged institutional prudence in deferring to the STF, given ongoing challenges to the calendar, including cases from other states.

item.title: Valdemar justifica ‘momento difícil’ para saída de Michelle do PL Mulher
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro resigns as national president of PL Women amid a 'difficult moment' cited by Valdemar Costa Neto, choosing to focus full-time on caring for jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro and addressing family tensions. Her departure follows a public video accusation against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for mistreatment, intensifying internal strife within the Bolsonaro clan.

item.title: Motta agradece a Lula e diz que Plano Safra ajuda produtores de cana
item.description: House President Hugo Motta thanked President Lula for the 2026/2027 Harvest Plan, stating it will aid 17,000 independent sugarcane producers in the Northeast impacted by U.S. tariffs, falling domestic sugar prices, and rising input costs. The plan allocates R$ 97.3 billion for family farming, including rural credit, agricultural insurance, and technical assistance.

item.title: TSE mantém diploma de deputado federal de Rondônia
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously upheld the diploma of federal deputy Rafael Bento Pereira, known as Rafael Fera, rejecting a challenge by the Electoral Public Ministry alleging ineligibility due to loss of his municipal mandate for breach of parliamentary decorum. The rapporteur, Minister Antonio Carlos Ferreira, ruled that ineligibility can only be based on facts occurring before the final candidate registration deadline for the 2022 elections, and the decree causing the loss of his mandate was issued after that deadline, making it ineligible to contest the diploma.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro deixa PL Mulher em meio a crise com Flávio
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro announced her resignation as national president of PL Mulher following internal conflicts with her stepson, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, over party alliances, particularly the PL’s alignment with Ciro Gomes in Ceará. Despite stepping down, the Liberal Party still views her as a potential Senate candidate for the Federal District, and her decision was made after a meeting with Valdemar Costa Neto and reflection with Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest.

item.title: “Melhor arma que um país pode ter é alimento”, diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defended food sovereignty as a country's 'best weapon' during the launch of the 2026/2027 Harvest Plan, announcing R$ 97.7 billion in credit for family farmers. He emphasized diversified food production, reduced rural credit interest rates, and the use of Union-held lands to strengthen family agriculture, referencing his conversation with Hugo Chávez on the need for food independence.

item.title: “Os maiores inimigos do Brasil são os políticos do Nordeste”, diz Renan Santos
item.description: Renan Santos, a pre-candidate for Presidency from Missão, stated that Brazil's biggest enemies are politicians from the Northeast, during a speech in Porto Alegre about the federal pact. He criticized the distribution of resources between the Union, states, and municipalities, blaming national problems on the region. The remark sparked controversy and was first published by O Antagonista.

item.title: Valdemar: Michelle deixou PL Mulher para concentrar atividades em cuidar do nosso presidente
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, national president of the Liberal Party (PL), stated that Michelle Bolsonaro left PL Mulher to focus on caring for former president Jair Bolsonaro. He described the decision as natural and acknowledged growing divisions within the party as expected. The remarks were made following a meeting in Brasília on Tuesday, the 30th.

item.title: Lula brinca com jogo Brasil x Japão e agradece publicamente Ancelotti
item.description: Lula joked about Brazil's 2-1 win over Japan during the launch of the Plano Safra/2026/27, praising Casemiro's goal and publicly thanking Carlo Ancelotti for not substituting the Brazilian midfielder. The event took place at the Palácio do Planalto on Tuesday, June 30.

item.title: PT tenta atrair eleitorado católico
item.description: The PT will release on Wednesday, May 1st, a letter addressed to Catholics, drafted following a Tuesday night meeting on April 30th, as part of a strategy to attract religious voters, similar to the approach taken on June 8th with evangelicals. The text focuses on faith and values but explicitly excludes the abortion issue, aiming to broaden Catholic support in Lula’s re-election bid.

item.title: Justiça Eleitoral alinha estratégias de TI e segurança para as Eleições 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) convened IT secretaries from all 27 Regional Electoral Courts (TREs) to align technology and security strategies for the 2026 General Elections. The meeting focused on refining risk mitigation and contingency plans, covering cyberattack prevention, logistical and electronic security, network infrastructure, and rapid response to operational incidents.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil fará "tudo ao alcance" para ajudar Venezuela
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil will do "everything within its reach" to assist Venezuela following earthquakes that left nearly 2,000 dead. He announced the deployment of Brazilian Air Force aircraft carrying rescue teams, health professionals, and humanitarian aid, and emphasized a ministerial delegation led by Defense Minister José Múcio to coordinate relief and reconstruction efforts.

item.title: Atos de sindicatos pelo país pedem o fim da escala 6 X 1
item.description: Workers from 15 states and the Federal District held protests on Tuesday (June 30, 2026) demanding the end of the 6x1 work scale and approval of PEC 221/2019 in the Senate, which would reduce the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours. The movement, led by unions including CUT, Frentes Brasil Popular and VAT, had modest turnout in Brasília (around 200 people), with speeches by Agnelo Queiroz and Leandro Grass criticizing the elite and advocating for workers’ rest and health.

item.title: Lula aposta em vitória do Brasil por 3x0 contra Noruega e agradece Ancelotti por ter mantido Casemiro em campo contra o Japão
item.description: President Lula predicted Brazil will defeat Norway 3-0 in the 2026 World Cup round of 16, set for July 5 in New Jersey. He also praised coach Carlo Ancelotti for keeping Casemiro on the field during the match against Japan, noting the midfielder’s goal after early criticism. Lula emphasized that trusting Ancelotti’s judgment paid off despite initial doubts.
